subject: Data isolation boundary confirmation — Dedicated vs Private VPC next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@medisyshealth.com>, Rajiv Sen <rajiv.sen@medisyshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — isolation expectations and clarification items

Hi Helen / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the two clarifying items we need to qualify whether Dedicated capacity or a Private VPC is the right fit for MediSys: 

1) Data residency & custody: you said patient PHI cannot leave your cloud tenancy and you require customer-managed keystore for all encryption keys. That strongly indicates Private VPC (private control plane or on-prem) rather than Hosted/Dedicated, but I want to confirm whether a Private control plane (Redwood appliances in your VPC) is acceptable or you need fully air-gapped on-prem.

2) Control plane visibility & audit: you asked for audit logs, keystore access logs, and SOC2 evidence. We can provide SOC2 + the keystore residency options, but we need to know if your procurement wants snapshots of audit logs pushed to your Splunk (S3 delivery) or if periodic attestations are sufficient.

Next steps I propose: 
- You confirm: (A) Private control plane acceptable? (B) KMS: BYOK/HSM required? (C) Required cadence for audit delivery?
- I’ll loop in Ben (sales engineering) and Karthik (solutions) to prepare an evidence packet and a simple ops playbook for whichever path you choose.

I attached a short spec sheet for our Dedicated offering for reference (redwood-dedicated-specs.pdf). If Private is the direction, Ben will prepare the isolation-evidence-checklist.

Target: align on path by end of week so we can scope a POC and pricing.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0167

Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference runtime
From: Helen Park <helen.park@medisyshealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Sen <rajiv.sen@medisyshealth.com>, procurement@medisyshealth.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — isolation expectations and clarification items

Jonas —

Thanks for the recap. A couple quick answers: 

A) Private control plane is acceptable; preferred, actually. We would rather Redwood’s control plane live in our VPC and talk to the inference nodes that are also deployed in the same VPC. Full air-gapped on-prem would be a second option but will add more procurement friction.

B) KMS: BYOK with HSM-backed keys is required for encryption-at-rest. The keystore must be in our cloud account and we must be able to rotate keys on our schedule.

C) Audit logs: we prefer log delivery to our S3 bucket (daily bundle) and immediate copies to our SIEM for any failed auth attempts. Weekly attestations are not sufficient for our security team.

If Ben or Karthik need anything from our IT/security, let us know. I’ve copied procurement for contracting timelines.

—Helen
Head of Cloud Ops, MediSys Health
helen.park@medisyshealth.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@medisyshealth.com>, Rajiv Sen <rajiv.sen@medisyshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — isolation expectations and clarification items

Helen — great, thanks for the clear answers. Summary based on your notes and what we’ll deliver for a Private VPC path: 

- Deployment model: Private VPC with control plane components deployed as customer-managed (private control plane) inside your cloud tenancy. Inference nodes will be provisioned in your VPC/subnets with strict security groups and restricted egress.
- KMS/Keystore: BYOK is supported. We can integrate with your cloud KMS (HSM-backed). Keys remain in your account; Redwood stores only key references and never the raw key material. You retain key rotation and policies.
- Audit logs: We will configure daily S3 delivery of the control plane + node audit bundles and set up an event stream for failed auth alerts to your SIEM. We will also produce weekly attestations for contractual purposes.

What I need from you to scope the POC and draft contract language: 
1) Desired subnet/CIDR ranges and whether the control plane should be in the same subnets as inference nodes or a dedicated management subnet.
2) Example S3 bucket name/permissions for log delivery and the SIEM ingestion endpoint (ARN / endpoint).
3) Security contact for an HSM/BYOK integration call (I suggest we schedule a 30-min technical touchpoint this week).

I’ve attached the isolation-evidence-checklist.xlsx that Ben prepared; it lists the concrete artifacts we can supply (audit samples, SOC2 sections, network diagrams, encryption flowchart). Ben / Karthik — can you confirm availability for a technical call today or tomorrow?

Thanks —
Jonas

---
Attachment: isolation-evidence-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub: columns for artifact, owner, expected delivery)
From: Rajiv Sen <rajiv.sen@medisyshealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Helen Park <helen.park@medisyshealth.com>
Cc: procurement@medisyshealth.com
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 10:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — isolation expectations and clarification items

Thanks Jonas — that matches our expectations.

Procurement: we are moving forward with Private VPC (control plane inside our tenancy) pending standard legal language on SLAs and data custody. Please include the HSM/BYOK appendix and the daily S3 audit delivery clause.

Helen — I’ll send the subnet/CIDR details and SIEM endpoint by EOD.

-Rajiv
VP, Infrastructure, MediSys Health
rajiv.sen@medisyshealth.com
